description: Identical-data production-stack step-0 loss/grad comparison (8-GPU FSDP SFT). Step-0 loss is the pre-optimizer-step global-mean over the effective batch; grad_norm is pre-clip fp32 global all-reduced. lr is the warmup init.
conclusion: With identical step-0 data (data.loader_mode=reference_fanout) the RLinf production step-0 loss matches the reference within abs 0.0044 (< the 0.01 bf16 band) and grad_norm collapses from 6.69 to 2.35 (~reference 2.17), vs the decentralized default's 0.327/6.69. So the first-step loss+grad gap is DATA-SIDE (the decentralized loader feeds different step-0 data). The remaining grad residual (rel ~8%) is the production noise/time DRAW differing between repos, not a compute defect: the model compute_loss is byte-identical (vendored) and same-batch+noise parity is confirmed by the cross-feed (phase6_ac3_cross_feed.json).
grad_residual_note: The 8.05% fanout-vs-reference grad residual is the LIVE production noise/time draw differing between repos (each samples its own at step 0); the mean loss is noise-robust (256-sample mean) so it matches within 0.0044, but the grad is noise-sensitive. The production identical-data grad WITHIN tolerance (matched noise) is in phase6_ac3_cross_feed_2x2.json: ref-batch column grad rel 0.029% <= 2% (both production stacks on identical data + shared noise).
